newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk textile group Akkok sees '96 sales target met.
newsitem.headline: Turk textile group Akkok sees '96 sales target met.

text.p: Turkey's major textile and chemicals producer Akkok Group of Companies said on Wednesday it would meet its 1996 sales target of $935 million after good performance in the eight-month results.
"We have had very good results in our sales in the domestic market," said Omer Dinckok, president of the group.
"We realised almost all of our $150-million export target for 1996. All these go to show that we will reach 1996 sales target of $935 million," he told Reuters in an interview.
Dinckok, also the president of the Istanbul Chamber of Industry, said their investments for 1996, worth $52 million and in the areas of energy and textile, were underway as planned.
"We completed a total $192 million investment in the 1993-95 period, all realised without any loans," he said.

The group made 46 percent of its turnover from textiles, 42 percent from chemicals, six percent from energy and the rest from its other business including real estate development, marketing and management, and retailing.

The group will allot 30 percent of this year's planned investment to a power and steam cogeneration unit -- Akenerji Elektrik Uretimi Otoproduktor Grubu A.S -- to raise its established capacity to 285 MegaWatts (MW) from 125 MW.
Akenerji supplies power and steam to the group's plants and 77 other industrial companies.

The rest of the investment will be spent for plans to modernise and expand capacity in the group's textile plants Aksu Iplik Dokuma ve Boya Apre Fabrikalari A.S., Akal Tekstil Sanayii A.S., and chemicals producers Aksa Akrilik Kimya Sanayii A.S., Akkim Kimya Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S.
When the investments have been completed, the total acrylic fiber capacity of the group would increase five percent to 210,000 tonnes per year, Dinckok said.
He said output capacities of yarn (53,000 tonnes/year) and fabric (4.5 million metres/year) will also be increased with the investments.

The group has a chemicals output capacity of 145,000 tonnes. It can produce 1,335,000 pieces of blanket a year, 8.5 million square metres of wall-to-wall carpets, 112,000 cubic metres polyurethane foam and 530 tonnes of steam.
Dinckok said the chemicals company Aksa was targeting to raise its market penetration and develop higher value added products in 1997 but gave no details.
The group's Akal company has a 40 percent share in the domestic worsted-yarn market and 70 percent in semi-worsted yarn market.
Akal will invest $20 million to renovate its plant in Yalova, near Istanbul, after completing a similar project worth $15 million in its Alapli plant on the Black Sea this year.
Akal's share price closed at 6,100 lira on Wednesday, unchanged from a day earlier. That of Aksu was 5,100 lira, up 150 lira, and Aksa 20,750 lira, up 1,500 lira.
